title: Synthesis of New Lithium Ionic Conductor Thio-LISICON—Lithium Silicon Sulfides System

structure.title: Abstract / Introduction
structure.text:
Masahiro Murayama,\*,† Ryoji Kanno,\*,¹ Michihiko Irie,† Shinya Ito,† Takayuki Hata,† Noriyuki Sonoyama,\* and Yoji Kawamoto†

Received February 19, 2002; in revised form May 28, 2002; accepted July 15, 2002

The new lithium ionic conductors, thio-LISICON (LIthium SuperIonic CONductor), were found in the ternary Li<sub>2</sub>S-SiS<sub>2</sub>-Al<sub>2</sub>S<sub>3</sub> and Li<sub>2</sub>S-SiS<sub>2</sub>-P<sub>2</sub>S<sub>5</sub> systems. Their structures of new materials, Li<sub>4+x</sub>Si<sub>1-x</sub>Al<sub>x</sub>S<sub>4</sub> and Li<sub>4-x</sub>Si<sub>1-x</sub>P<sub>x</sub>S<sub>4</sub> were determined by X-ray Rietveld analysis, and the electric and electrochemical properties were studied by electronic conductivity, ac conductivity and cyclic voltammogram measurements. The structure of the host material, Li<sub>4</sub>SiS<sub>4</sub> is related to the γ-Li<sub>3</sub>PO<sub>4</sub>-type structure, and when the Li<sup>+</sup> interstitials or Li<sup>+</sup> vacancies were created by the partial substitutions of Al<sup>3+</sup> or P<sup>5+</sup> for Si<sup>4+</sup>, large increases in conductivity occur. The solid solution member x = 0.6 in  $\text{Li}_{4-x}\text{Si}_{1-x}P_xS_4$  showed high conductivity of  $6.4 \times 10^{-4}\,\text{S cm}^{-1}$  at  $27^{\circ}\text{C}$  with negligible electronic conductivity. The new solid solution, Li<sub>4-r</sub>Si<sub>1-r</sub>P<sub>r</sub>S<sub>4</sub>, also has high electrochemical stability up to  $\sim 5 \, \mathrm{V}$  vs Li at room temperature. All-solid-state lithium cells were investigated using the  $Li_{3.4}Si_{0.4}P_{0.6}S_4$  electrolyte,  $LiCoO_2$  cathode and In anode. © 2002 Elsevier Science (USA)

structure.title: INTRODUCTION
structure.text:
Lithium superionic conductors are of technological importance for future applications as solid electrolytes for all-solid-state lithium batteries and may solve the safety problems of the rechargeable lithium ion batteries using non-aqueous liquid electrolytes (1). Ceramic crystalline electrolytes have advantages over liquid, polymer, gel or even glass electrolytes for their chemical and electrochemical stability. Many attempts to synthesize new ceramic lithium superionic conductors have been made; the highest

conductivity of  $10^{-3} \, \mathrm{S} \, \mathrm{cm}^{-1}$  was previously reported for H-doped Li<sub>3</sub>N (2). However, the low decomposition potential of  $\sim 0.445 \, \mathrm{V}$  restricts its application as a lithium solid electrolyte (3). In order to improve the stability of the solid electrolytes, a material search is still necessary, and this includes ceramic crystalline materials.

A wide variety of materials have been synthesized in the LISICON [Li<sub>14</sub>Zn(GeO<sub>4</sub>)<sub>4</sub>] (4) system. The structure is related to the  $\gamma$ -Li<sub>3</sub>PO<sub>4</sub> type, and is formed by LiO<sub>4</sub>, GeO<sub>4</sub>, SiO<sub>4</sub>, PO<sub>4</sub>, ZnO<sub>4</sub>, VO<sub>4</sub> tetrahedra or LiO<sub>6</sub> octahedra. A wide range of solid solutions formed by aliovalent substitutions introduced interstitial lithium ions or lithium vacancies, and led to high ionic conductivities at higher temperatures (5). However, the conductivity values at room temperature ( $\sim 10^{-6} \, \mathrm{S \, cm^{-1}}$  for Li<sub>3.6</sub>Si<sub>0.6</sub>P<sub>0.4</sub>O<sub>4</sub> (6, 7), for example) are still lower than those of copper and silver ionic conductors (8–10).

In order to modify the materials to attain high ionic conductivity, sulfides have a number of advantages over oxides for constructing ionic conductors; i.e., larger ionic radii and more polarizable character of sulfide ions may improve the mobility of the conduction species. Generally speaking, crystalline materials should have higher conductivity than the corresponding glasses, if their crystal structures have been well designed for high ionic conduction. For example, the highest crystalline ionic conductive solids,  $Rb_4Cu_{16}I_7Cl_{13}$  (8, 9) and  $RbAg_4I_5$  (10), have much higher ionic conductivity than any copper and silver conducting glasses (11). Furthermore, another advantage of crystalline materials is their stability at high temperature. However, inorganic crystalline lithium ion conductors have usually lower conductivities than those of glasses. New material search is still necessary to find high lithium ionic conducting crystalline compounds. Only a few materials have been investigated previously in the crystalline sulfides;  $Li_3PS_4$  (12, 13),  $Li_4SiS_4$  (14) and  $Li_2SiS_3$  (14)

were reported to have conductivities of  $10^{-7}$ – $10^{-9}$  S cm<sup>-1</sup> at room temperature, and no systematic material search has been made.

We found recently the new lithium ionic conductors, thio-LISICON based on the lithium germanium sulfides (15, 16). These compounds have host structures similar to the  $\gamma$ -Li<sub>3</sub>PO<sub>4</sub> type, and the conductivities are in the order of  $10^{-5}$ – $10^{-3}$  S cm<sup>-1</sup> at room temperature. This indicates that there may exist a wide variety of materials in the thio-LISICON system. In the present study, new material search is carried out based on the lithium silicon sulfides, Li<sub>4</sub>SiS<sub>4</sub>, and new solid solutions were found in the Li<sub>2</sub>S–SiS<sub>2</sub>–Al<sub>2</sub>S<sub>3</sub> and Li<sub>2</sub>S-SiS<sub>2</sub>–P<sub>2</sub>S<sub>5</sub> systems with the family of thio-LISICON.

nodes.title: Rationale for Sulfide and Crystalline Conductors
nodes.text: In order to modify the materials to attain high ionic conductivity, sulfides have a number of advantages over oxides for constructing ionic conductors; i.e., larger ionic radii and more polarizable character of sulfide ions may improve the mobility of the conduction species. Generally speaking, crystalline materials should have higher conductivity than the corresponding glasses, if their crystal structures have been well designed for high ionic conduction. For example, the highest crystalline ionic conductive solids,  $Rb_4Cu_{16}I_7Cl_{13}$  (8, 9) and  $RbAg_4I_5$  (10), have much higher ionic conductivity than any copper and silver conducting glasses (11). Furthermore, another advantage of crystalline materials is their stability at high temperature. However, inorganic crystalline lithium ion conductors have usually lower conductivities than those of glasses. New material search is still necessary to find high lithium ionic conducting crystalline compounds.

structure.title: **EXPERIMENTAL**
structure.text:
The starting materials were Li<sub>2</sub>S, Al<sub>2</sub>S<sub>3</sub>, and P<sub>2</sub>S<sub>5</sub> (Kojundo Chemical Laboratory, >99.9% purity) and SiS<sub>2</sub> (Soekawa Chemicals, >95% purity). These were weighed, mixed in appropriate molar ratios in an argon-filled glove box, put into a carbon-coated quartz tube and heated at a reaction temperature of  $700^{\circ}$ C for 8 h. After the reaction, the tube was slowly cooled to room temperature.

X-ray diffraction patterns of the powdered samples were obtained with an X-ray diffractometer (Rigaku RU-200B, 12 kW) with Cu $K\alpha$  radiation. The diffraction data were collected at each  $0.02^{\circ}$  step width over a  $2\theta$  range from  $20^{\circ}$  to  $110^{\circ}$ . The lattice parameters and structures of the solid solutions, Li<sub>4+x</sub>Si<sub>1-x</sub>Al<sub>x</sub>S<sub>4</sub> and Li<sub>4-x</sub>Si<sub>1-x</sub>P<sub>x</sub>S<sub>4</sub> were refined by X-ray Rietveld analysis using the computer programs, RIETAN-2000 (17).

Ionic conductivity was measured by ac impedance methods in a nitrogen gas flow over a  $25^{\circ}\text{C} \leq t \leq 300^{\circ}\text{C}$  temperature range with an applied frequency range of  $10\,\text{Hz}$  and  $1\,\text{MHz}$  using a Solartron 1260 frequency response analyzer. A gold paste used for blocking electrode was painted onto both sides of a sample, and the sample was then heated under vacuum at  $150^{\circ}\text{C}$  for  $3\,\text{h}$ . Measurements were carried out for the samples with a pellet (8 mm diameter and  $2\text{--}3\,\text{mm}$  thick), and with a rectangular shape  $(5\times 6\times 2.5\,\text{mm}^3)$  for the solid solutions,  $\text{Li}_{4+x}\text{Si}_{1-x}\text{Al}_x\text{S4}$  and  $\text{Li}_{4-x}\text{Si}_{1-x}P_x\text{S4}$ , respectively.

Cyclic voltammogram (CV) of the asymmetric Li/Li<sub>4-x</sub>Si<sub>1-x</sub>P<sub>x</sub>S<sub>4</sub> /Au cell was examined using a reference lithium electrode with the scan rate of 1–10 mV s<sup>-1</sup> and the scan range between -0.2 and 5 V using a Solartron 1287 electrochemical interface.

Electrochemical cells with  $LiCoO_2$  and In electrodes were constructed to investigate the cell performances using the new thio-LISICON electrolyte. The electrolyte powder was pressed into a pellet with a diameter of  $10 \, \text{mm}$  and thickness of  $1 \, \text{mm}$ . The positive electrode material is a mixture of  $LiCoO_2$  and electrolyte powder in a weight ratio

of 1:1. The electrode was pressed together with the electrolyte layer into a two-layered pellet. The charge–discharge curves were measured by constant currents ranging from 10 to  $100 \,\mu A$ .

structure.title: Synthesis and Structures
structure.text:
The Host Material, Li<sub>4</sub>SiS<sub>4</sub>

In the binary Li<sub>2</sub>S-SiS<sub>2</sub> system, two compounds, Li<sub>2</sub>SiS<sub>3</sub> and Li<sub>4</sub>SiS<sub>4</sub>, were reported to exist previously, and their structure models were proposed (14). The X-ray diffraction pattern of Li<sub>4</sub>SiS<sub>4</sub> was quite similar to that of Li<sub>4</sub>SiO<sub>4</sub> with the γ-Li<sub>3</sub>PO<sub>4</sub>-type structure; the structure was refined using the structure model of Li<sub>4</sub>SiO<sub>4</sub> (18, 19). Table 1 lists the final R factors, lattice and structural parameters with their estimated standard deviations in parentheses. Because of the low scattering factor of Li, the Li positions were not included in the refinements. The results confirmed the  $\gamma$ -Li<sub>3</sub>PO<sub>4</sub>-type structure similar to that of Li<sub>4</sub>GeS<sub>4</sub> (20). Figure 1 shows the structure of Li<sub>4</sub>SiS<sub>4</sub>. The structure is composed of hexagonal closely packed sulfide ion arrays. The silicon ions are distributed over the tetrahedral sites, and the SiS<sub>4</sub> tetrahedra are isolated from each other. Further study based on neutron diffraction is necessary to clarify the Li positions.

In our material synthesis based on the stoichiometric  $\text{Li}_4\text{SiS}_4$ , solid solutions were examined by aliovalent substitutions,  $\text{Si}^{4+}\leftrightarrow \text{Li}^++\text{Al}^{3+}$  or  $\text{Si}^{4+}+\text{Li}^+\leftrightarrow \text{P}^{5+}$ ; this may lead interstitial lithium ions or lithium vacancies according to the formulae,  $\text{Li}_{4+x}\text{Si}_{1-x}\text{Al}_x\text{S4}$ , and  $\text{Li}_{4-x}\text{Si}_{1-x}\text{P}_x\text{S4}$ , respectively.

structure.text: The new solid solution was synthesized along the tie line between $\text{Li}_4\text{SiS}_4$ and $\text{Li}_3\text{PS}_4$ in the ternary $\text{Li}_2\text{S}-\text{SiS}_2-\text{P}_2\text{S}_5$ system. The samples synthesized according to the formulae, $\text{Li}_{4-x}\text{Si}_{1-x}\text{P}_x\text{S}_4$ , showed diffraction patterns similar to the corresponding oxide, $\text{Li}_4\text{SiO}_4$ . Figure 2 shows the X-ray TABLE 1 X-Ray Rietveld Refinement Results for Li4SiS4 | Atom | Site | g | x | y | z | $B(\mathring{A}^2)$ | |-------|------|---|-------------|------------|-------------|---------------------| | Si | 2e | 1 | 0.6737 (11) | 0.25 | 0.3612 (12) | 0.22 (19) | | S (1) | 4f | 1 | 0.8121 (6) | 0.0200 (6) | 0.2381 (8) | 0.63 (15) | | S (2) | 2e | 1 | 0.3657 (9) | 0.25 | 0.2360 (13) | 1.3 (2) | | S (3) | 2e | 1 | 0.6757 (10) | 0.25 | 0.7126 (12) | 1.3 (2) | Note. $P2_1/m$ , a = 6.8934(3) Å, b = 7.7675(3) Å, c = 6.1241(2) Å, $\beta = 91.225(5)^\circ$ , $R_{\rm wp} = 11.26\%$ , $R_{\rm p} = 8.72\%$ , $R_{\rm R} = 18.25\%$ , $R_{\rm e} = 5.93\%$ , $R_{\rm I} = 5.97\%$ , $R_{\rm F} = 2.75\%$ , $S = R_{\rm wp}/R_{\rm e} = 1.89$ . ![](_page_2_Picture_2.jpeg) FIG. 1. Structure of Li4SiS4. Only SiS4 tetrahedra is indicated in the figure. diffraction patterns for the ternary Li2S–SiS2–P2S5 system. The diffraction patterns showed continuous shift in the diffraction lines from Li4SiS4 to Li3PS4, which suggests the formation of a solid solution in the whole composition range. A careful analysis of the diffraction data, however, indicated an appearance of superlattice reflections. The patterns in the solid solution were indexed assuming a monoclinic superlattice cell of $2a \times 3b \times 2c$ which is related to the parent lattice $(a \times b \times c)$ of the host material, Li4SiS4. In the new solid solution, Li4-x- $Si_{1-x}P_xS_4$ , the $2a \times 3b \times 2c$ superlattice with space group $P2_1/m$ was used for the refinements of the lattice parameters. Figure 3 illustrates the fitted profile and difference patterns for $\text{Li}_{4-x}\text{Si}_{1-x}\text{P}_x\text{S}_4$ with x = 0.8. Although, the fitting of the pattern is not good enough to solve all the structure parameters, the existence of the superlattice was confirmed. Further studies based on neutron diffraction are necessary. Figure 4 shows the composition dependence of the lattice parameters in $\text{Li}_{4-x}\text{Si}_{1-x}P_x\text{S}_4$ . The lattice parameters plotted in Figure 4 are based on the parent lattice of $\text{Li}_4\text{SiS}_4$ with the $a \times b \times c$ cells. Table 2 summarizes the lattice parameter values of $\text{Li}_{4-x}\text{Si}_{1-x}P_x\text{S}_4$ . The same type of supperlattice reflections was observed for the solid solution of the thio-LISICON, $\text{Li}_{4-x}\text{Ge}_{1-x}P_x\text{S}_4$ (15). The formation of the superlattice in $\text{Li}_{4-x}\text{Ge}_{1-x}P_x\text{S}_4$ was more complex; the solid solution was divided into three regions; the region I $(0 < x \le 0.6)$ were indexed with a monoclinic superlattice cell of $a \times 3b \times 2c$ , the region II (0.6 < x < 0.8) with $a \times 3b \times 3c$ , and the region III $(0.8 \le x < 1.0)$ with $a \times 2b \times 2c$ cell. These regions of the monoclinic superstructures might correspond to different types of cation ordering. The diffraction data in both systems indicated the formations of the solid solutions in the whole composition range. Neutron diffraction studies are necessary to clarify the structural details on the lithium positions and the origin of the superlattice reflections.

structure.text: The Ternary Li2S-SiS2-P2S5 System Ionic conductivity was measured with an ac impedance method over a $25^{\circ}$ C $< t < 300^{\circ}$ C temperature range with an applied frequency range of 10 Hz–1 MHz. The conductivity values were determined from the impedance plots of the data. Figures 7(a) and 7(b) show the impedance plots of $\text{Li}_{4-x}\text{Si}_{1-x}\text{P}_x\text{S}_4$ with x=0.4 and 0.6, respectively. A semicircle was observed for the sample, x = 0.4, at 25°C in the high-frequency range with a spike in the lowfrequency range which is caused by an electrode contribution (Fig. 7(a)). The semicircle was interpreted as a parallel combination of a resistance and a capacitance, and is attributed to the bulk and grain boundary contribution, which was estimated by those capacitance values of $10^{-9}$ $10^{-10}$ F, and the spike to the electrode contribution. However, the bulk and grain boundary contributions could not be separated. At high temperature, no semicircle was observed and only a spike caused by the electrode contribution was observed. For the sample, x = 0.6 in $Li_{4-x}Si_{1-x}P_xS_4$ , only a spike caused by an electrode contribution was observed even at 27°C (Fig. 7(b)). The behavior of the impedance plots shows the characteristics of a pure ionic conductor composed of bulk and electrode contributions where the bulk resistance values were calculated from the intercept of the spike. No differences in conductivities were observed between the cooling and heating process during the measurements. structure.title: Comparison with Other Ionic Conductors
structure.text: In aliovalent solid solution, ions are substituted by other ions of different charge, which causes consequently additional changes involving creation of vacancies or interstitials (ionic compensation), or electrons or holes (electronic compensation) to preserve electroneutrality. It is reasonable to assume the former mechanism because no transition elements exist as a constituent of the thio-LISICON, which likely forms pure ionic conduction as a ![](_page_5_Figure_2.jpeg) **FIG. 6.** Lattice parameter changes in $Li_{4+x}Si_{1-x}Al_xS_4$ . result. The partial substitution of P5+ for Si4+ may introduce lithium vacancy, and increase the conductivity. The conductivity value of the new thio-LISICON $(6.4 \times 10^{-4} \,\mathrm{S\,cm^{-1}}$ at 27°C) is much higher than those of the oxide LISICON, Li14Zn(GeO4)4 (4) and Li3.6Si0.6P0.4O4 (6, 7) by two or three orders of magnitude. The conductivity-value is also comparable to those of the previous ceramic lithium superionic conductors, the intrinsic Li3N $(2-4\times10^{-4}\,\mathrm{S\,cm}^{-1})$ (2), H-doped Li3N $(6 \times 10^{-3} \,\mathrm{S\,cm}^{-1})$ (2) and $La_{0.62}Li_{0.16}TiO_3$ (1 × 10-4 S cm-1) (21), and the modified sulfide glasses, Li2S-SiS2-LiI $(1.8 \times 10^{-3} \,\mathrm{S\,cm}^{-1})$ (22) and Li2S–SiS2–Li3PO4 (6.9 × 10-4) S cm-1) (23). Among the thio-LISICON compounds, the conductivity-value of the new solid solution, Li4-x $Si_{1-x}P_xS_4$ is of one order magnitude lower than that of Li4-xGe1-xPxS4, which showed the highest conductivity of $2.2 \times 10^{-3} \,\mathrm{S \, cm^{-1}}$ at room temperature (15).

structure.title: CONCLUSION
structure.text: The new thio-LISICON compounds based on lithium silicon sulfides were found to exist and to have a high ionic conductivity of  $6.4 \times 10^{-4}\,\mathrm{S\,cm^{-1}}$  at room temperature for  $\mathrm{Li_{3.4}Si_{0.4}P_{0.6}S_4}$ . The material shows high electrochemical stability and no reaction with lithium metal. Based on the stoichiometric  $\mathrm{Li_{4}SiS_{4}}$ , lithium vacancies and interstitial lithium ions were introduced by aliovalent substitutions of  $\mathrm{Si^{4+}} \Leftrightarrow \mathrm{Li^{+}} + \mathrm{Al^{3+}}$  and  $\mathrm{Si^{4+}} + \mathrm{Li^{+}} \Leftrightarrow \mathrm{P^{5+}}$ , respectively. The conductivity increased in both substitutions. An all-solid-state lithium cell using  $\mathrm{In/Li_{3.4}Si_{0.4}P_{0.6}S_4/LiCoO_2}$  was operated at high voltage (4.5 V). The cell was charged and discharged at currents of  $> 127\,\mu\mathrm{A\,cm^{-2}}$ .
